key_insights.insight: The default customer path remains the standard workflow control plane, and that path is materially aligned across the desktop UI, gateway routes, and backend workflow endpoints.

The uiBridge feature is customer-visible but not fully wired: config surfaces expose gateway.ui_bridge_enabled, while the runtime gate still only reads NIKO_UI_BRIDGE_ENABLED during gateway control-plane initialization.

Checkpoint list/create/restore bypass the workspace authority model that already protects plan, execute, lifecycle, and quick rollback, creating a real control-plane seam on customer-facing restore surfaces.

key_findings.finding: uiBridge config-source drift is real, not hypothetical. The backend advertises gateway.ui_bridge_enabled in both the modifiable-field contract and the desktop config schema, but the actual route gate is a module-level boolean set only by setUiBridgeEnabled(process.env.NIKO_UI_BRIDGE_ENABLED === 'true'). resolveUiBridgeEnabled() exists and supports config fallback, yet is unused by the running gate.
key_findings.impact: If a customer switches workflowBackendMode to uiBridge in Settings, the frontend will call /ui-bridge/workflow/* and can receive 403 disabled responses even after saving backend config or reloading config. This is a pre-delivery product seam, but it only affects the optional uiBridge path because the shipped default remains standard mode.

key_findings.finding: The checkpoint authority gap is broader than exploration first implied. checkpoint/create, checkpoint/list, and checkpoint/restore neither resolve workspace payloads nor pass authority into the workflow engine, while quick rollback does. Engine restoreCheckpoint() and listCheckpoints() operate on the gateway-global checkpoint map by checkpoint id alone.
key_findings.impact: Evaluation, app-level checkpoint menu, and chat-recovery surfaces can enumerate and restore checkpoints outside the current workflow authority scope. Because restoreCheckpoint() can perform git checkout by commit hash without workspace binding, this is customer-blocking for any release that keeps checkpoint restore/recovery UI enabled.

key_findings.finding: The control-plane seam is bounded rather than systemic. Plan, execute, lifecycle, and quick rollback all derive workspace authority from the project workspace model and have dedicated workspace-binding tests; current integration tests confirm the main standard workflow path and current checkpoint endpoints still respond successfully.
key_findings.impact: Core authoring and workflow orchestration are substantially complete. The project is not a broad UI/API mismatch; delivery risk is concentrated in the uiBridge toggle and unscoped checkpoint restore surfaces.

discussion_points: If uiBridge is not part of the customer contract, should the team remove or relabel both workflowBackendMode=uiBridge and gateway.ui_bridge_enabled from customer-facing settings before delivery?

If checkpoint restore is intended only as an internal recovery/admin tool, should the desktop checkpoint menu and chat-recovery restore path be disabled for the customer build until authority scoping exists?
open_questions: Will customer delivery expose the full Settings backend-service section, or can unsupported control-plane toggles be hidden in the release profile?

Is the expected customer deployment strictly single-user/single-workspace at a time, or must checkpoint recovery remain safe across multiple concurrent conversations/workspaces within one gateway runtime?

recommendations.action: Treat checkpoint authority as a pre-delivery blocker: either thread workspace authority through checkpoint create/list/restore, or remove/disable all customer-facing checkpoint restore surfaces and force recovery through /workflow/rollback only.
recommendations.rationale: This is the only seam here that lets a customer-visible path mutate workspace state outside the authority model that governs the rest of the workflow control plane.

recommendations.action: Treat uiBridge as P1 before release: either wire the runtime gate to resolveUiBridgeEnabled() and refresh it from config initialization/reload, or hide/remove uiBridge options from customer-facing settings.
recommendations.rationale: The issue is real but scoped to a non-default optional mode. It becomes customer-blocking only if the mode is intentionally offered as supported behavior.

recommendations.action: Add explicit regression tests for config-driven uiBridge enablement and for checkpoint authority rejection across mismatched workspace/session contexts.
recommendations.rationale: Current tests prove route presence and happy paths, but they do not lock the two seam failures that most affect delivery confidence.
